tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to learn what the Treetracker Admin API does. It is the RESTful backend for the Greenstand Admin Panel, which verifies, processes, and manages tree-capture data collected by the Treetracker mobile app. The README gives the quick-start guide, code style rules, and Docker workflow that frame the rest of this tour.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: The production entry point constructs the ExpressServer, boots it, and starts listening for requests. The server module is an Express wrapper that mounts CORS, JSON parsing, the audit and auth middleware, static assets, and finally the LoopBack application. Together these two files show how a request reaches the framework.

tour.title: LoopBack 4 Application Core
tour.description: Building on the server from Step 2, the LoopBack application class wires the custom request-handling sequence, the REST explorer, and the boot components. The sequence file defines that pipeline through the MiddlewareSequence mixin. This is the heart of the framework: it discovers and binds controllers, repositories, and datasources at boot time.
tour.languageLesson: LoopBack 4 uses dependency injection and a boot phase: the Application class scans convention-based directories (controllers, repositories, models) and binds them into an IoC container, so wiring is declarative rather than manual.

tour.title: Configuration and Datasource
tour.description: The runtime config exposes the JWT secret and database settings read from environment variables. The datasource config supplies the PostgreSQL connection and a getDatasource helper, while the juggler datasource binding makes that connection injectable across every repository. These files are the foundation every data-access layer depends on.

tour.title: Domain Models
tour.description: The models barrel re-exports every domain entity for convenient import across controllers and repositories. Trees is the core capture record with geolocation, verification, and approval fields; Planter, Organization, and Species describe the people and taxonomy around each capture. These LoopBack models define the vocabulary the whole API speaks.

tour.title: Repositories and SQL Query Building
tour.description: The repositories barrel re-exports every repository for the controller layer. The Trees and Planter repositories add organization-scoped access control and custom find/count methods on top of the default LoopBack CRUD. The buildFilterQuery helper translates a LoopBack filter object into a parameterized SQL query, which is how the API supports rich filtering safely.
tour.languageLesson: Parameterized SQL (placeholders bound to values rather than string concatenation) prevents SQL injection while still letting callers compose dynamic where clauses and ordering.

tour.title: REST Controllers
tour.description: Controllers expose the HTTP surface. The controllers barrel lists them all, and the Trees controller is the richest: count, list, find-by-id, geospatial near-search, and a transactional update that emits domain events and publishes to RabbitMQ. The Planter and Organization controllers follow the same pattern with organization-scoped access checks.

tour.title: Authentication and Authorization
tour.description: The auth module provides login, JWT issuance, password hashing, and the isAuth middleware that enforces policy-based routing. The policy catalog defines named permissions for viewing and managing users, trees, and planters. The audit middleware decodes the JWT, inspects each request outcome, and records auditable actions to the database, giving the platform a full access-control and accountability layer.
tour.languageLesson: A JWT carries signed claims (like user id and role) that the server verifies with a shared secret on every request, so authorization decisions need no session lookup.

tour.title: Event-Driven Messaging with RabbitMQ
tour.description: When the Trees controller updates a capture it emits a domain event and publishes to a message broker. The RabbitMQ helper publishes a payload and handles the connection, while the messaging config defines the admin-verifications exchange. The DomainEvent model and repository persist each event payload and its processing status, giving the system a reliable, replayable event trail.
tour.languageLesson: Publishing events to a broker exchange decouples the API from downstream consumers: the controller does not wait on them, and persisted domain events let a consumer replay work after a failure.

tour.title: Database Migration
tour.description: The migration script boots the LoopBack application and runs schema migration to align the PostgreSQL tables with the models from Step 5. Running this is how a fresh environment gets a working database before the server starts serving requests.

tour.title: Integration Testing and Seeding
tour.description: The integration suite boots the ExpressServer, seeds the database, and exercises the tree, planter, and organization endpoints end to end. The seed fixture connects to the datasource and re-exports helpers to populate and clear tables between runs. This shows how the project verifies the layers from Steps 2 through 9 work together.

tour.title: Containerization and Local Stack
tour.description: The Dockerfile packages the API on a node:12 Alpine base, installing dependencies with npm ci and building the TypeScript. The local development compose stack composes the reverse proxy, admin web, and admin API containers with mounted source volumes, so a contributor can run the whole system with one command.
tour.languageLesson: docker-compose declares each service, its image or build context, and its dependencies; mounted source volumes let code changes appear inside the container without a rebuild, which speeds up local development.

tour.title: Kubernetes Deployment
tour.description: Production runs on Kubernetes managed with Kustomize. The base Deployment runs two replicas of the container, and SealedSecrets hold the encrypted database and RabbitMQ connection strings that decrypt into the cluster. This ties the code from earlier steps to how it actually runs in production.
tour.languageLesson: Kustomize layers environment-specific overlays over a shared base, so dev, test, and production reuse one manifest set with only image tags and secrets patched per environment.

tour.title: CI/CD Pipelines
tour.description: As a capstone, the build-and-deploy workflow lints, builds, and tests the API, then on push to master runs semantic-release and pushes the Docker image to DockerHub and updates the deployment overlay. The CodeQL workflow adds static security analysis on every push. These pipelines automate everything the earlier steps built.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows use `on` triggers to run `jobs` of sequential `steps`; a release job gated to the master branch keeps builds reproducible and deploys automatic.
